title: Multi-tenant data isolation

requirements.text: Every request resolves a tenant from trusted state, never from an unchecked client value
All reads and writes are filtered by tenant, so ids from another tenant behave as not found
The database enforces isolation (row-level security or equivalent), not only application code
Tests prove a user of tenant A cannot read or change tenant B's data

evidence.name: tenant context comes from the verified session and membership, never from an unchecked client value
tenant handler: 401, hidden 404 for foreign tenants
scoped queries add the tenant filter to every statement
scoped repository on PostgreSQL: ids from another tenant behave as not found
database enforcement: as app_user a raw unscoped SELECT returns only the current tenant
database enforcement: UPDATE and DELETE of another tenant
database enforcement: no tenant set returns 0 rows
inspectIsolation flags permissive policies that do not reference the tenant setting
cross-tenant test kit: assertTenantIsolation passes on an RLS table and fails on an unprotected one
end to end: a user of tenant A cannot read or change tenant B
test kit checks the tenant setting on one dedicated client

notes: module:tenant-isolation provides application-wide isolation: trusted tenant resolution, PostgreSQL row-level security (enabled and forced, transaction-local app.tenant_id, non-bypass app_user role), a tenant-scoped repository and a reusable cross-tenant test kit, proven on PGlite as a NOLOGIN NOBYPASSRLS role. Pooled multi-connection behavior, LOGIN roles and hosted Postgres are not fixture-verified, and non-PostgreSQL databases get application-level filtering only. Several feature packages (comments, rbac, chat, short-links) also scope their own tables by tenant.
